subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Agent Collaboration Enhancement: Capability Profiling + Shared Blackboard + Layered Memory + Token Cost Governance

question: Should OpenClaw pursue this full four-layer collaboration stack in core, decompose it into narrower canonical design tracks behind explicit core/plugin APIs, or move parts outside core to plugins/ClawHub?
rationale: The choice affects core agent dispatch, memory visibility, persistent state, config/default surfaces, provider cost admission, and security boundaries, so automation cannot safely pick the permanent product boundary.

options.title: Decompose into narrow tracks
options.body: Keep this as the umbrella RFC and approve only scoped child designs with explicit storage, security, plugin/API, and upgrade boundaries before code lands.

options.title: Approve a core collaboration stack
options.body: Treat the four layers as a core roadmap item and require a maintainer-authored architecture plan before implementation PRs.

options.title: Move optional pieces outside core
options.body: Close or narrow core work to missing APIs while capability routing, blackboards, and memory workflows ship as plugins or ClawHub packages when feasible.

recommendation.title: Decompose into narrow tracks
recommendation.body: Keep this as the umbrella RFC and approve only scoped child designs with explicit storage, security, plugin/API, and upgrade boundaries before code lands.

likelyOwner.reason: Steipete has already provided scoping guidance on related multi-agent work and is the clearest observed owner for the product-boundary decision.
